prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System (dry fuels, steep terrain, WUI). Baseline: segmentation, time sync, health checks, audit logs; coordination records keep timestamps, participants, radio path status. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): primary interface; common operating picture (perimeter, spread, resources, role symbology); produces Crew Staging Pin; records triage cases; holds jurisdictional constraints before Drone Pilot Operator briefing; marks failed radio route impaired (Orion acknowledges). North Lookout Camera Mast: smoke bearing; sends Thermal Spot Snippet. South Lookout Camera Mast: triangulation bearing; produces Camera Cleaning Log. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): keeps aircraft charged/ready; produces Battery Swap Ticket (to Drone Pilot Operator); must report launch readiness, aircraft health, recovery availability before recon release. Drone Tasking Service: converts objectives to missions (launch windows, image requirements, altitude limits, abort criteria); no flight-release authority; no launch conflicting with Marigold lanes. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): perimeter/heat/smoke/spot detection; compares recon, cameras, weather projections for tactical recommendations; may down-weight Smoke Classifier Module (supporting only, never sole basis for aircraft commitment). MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): weather fields; Wind Shift Bulletin (Redtail uses for sequencing, holding, drop direction). VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): fallback relay of approved aviation instructions when data degraded. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): tanker availability, ETA, turnaround, priority; must block plan release if approvals, airspace status or tanker readiness incomplete; produces Runway Release Note after runway validation. East Retardant Loading Pump (produces Retardant Batch Slip) and West Retardant Loading Pump: report state, flow readiness, out-of-service; loading status informational, not approval. Crewline Mobile Tablet: crew acknowledgements. Actors: County Emergency Liaison (sends Drone Corridor Permit). Duty Detection Officer (Orion): triage, escalation. Drone Pilot Operator: confirms route fits field conditions, no interference. Air Attack Supervisor (Redtail): reviews promoted location, confidence history, airspace before authorizing recon/retardant planning. Tanker Base Manager: checks batch slip vs assignment/quantity; resolves loading discrepancies before plan shown ready. States: Confirmed Ignition; Airspace Restricted limits dispatch until Redtail confirms route/altitude. Recon verifies

New part:
S146: The Crewline Mobile Tablet shows approved suppression objectives, aircraft caution areas, and current assignment notes for crews operating near the incident.
S147: The Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges nearby aircraft activity before personnel are moved into a drop zone or a reconnaissance overflight area.
S148: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console sends the Suppression Drop Receipt after a completed drop has been recorded and checked for required timing fields.
S149: During extended attack, the Caldera Incident Command Portal preserves each aviation decision with the approving supervisor, operational period, and reason for change.
S150: The County Emergency Liaison can view approved aviation status and public safety implications without gaining authority to alter dispatch or suppression records.
S151: If reconnaissance, loading status, or weather guidance conflicts with an active plan, the system holds the affected recommendation for Air Attack Supervisor review before further action.
S152: This section describes how helitack and ground crews receive assignments, staging information, hazards, and updated intelligence from the support system during active wildfire operations.
S153: When a held recommendation is cleared, the Air Attack Supervisor selects the operational intent in the Caldera Incident Command Portal.
S154: The Caldera Incident Command Portal records each assignment package with an objective, time validity, confirmation status, and required acknowledgments.
S155: The Crewline Mobile Tablet displays the current division assignment, route guidance, rally location, and assigned communications channel for the logged-in crew.
S156: The Helitack Crew Leader receives the same operational package with aviation constraints and landing zone notes after Air Attack Supervisor approval.
S157: Ground crew assignments are formatted for field execution and avoid analytic scores that are not needed for tactical movement.
S158: Staging information is maintained as georeferenced areas and route descriptions so that crews can confirm location without relying on informal landmarks.
S159: The Crewline Mobile Tablet caches the latest accepted staging information and marks any expired package as unavailable for execution.
S160: If the Confirmed Ignition State changes the perimeter or priority area, the Caldera Incident Command Portal marks affected crew assignments for review before release.
S161: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine updates hazard summaries when fire spread estimates, access constraints, or field observations change.
S162: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine applies the Ridge Shadow Mask when estimating crew-visible fire edge confidence in steep terrain.
S163: The Smoke Classifier Module uses the Camera Cleaning Log to suppress confidence changes caused by lens contamination and service timing.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
